facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2006 but lived together only for a short period. The relationship became strained and the wife left her husband's company. The husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(i-a) & (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, which was dismissed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: The court may not grant restitution of conjugal rights if the parties have been living separately for a long time.
legal_principles.held: Undisputably, after the Family Court had passed the ex-parte judgment against the appellant-wife in M.C.No.539/2007, the respondent-husband had remarried on 28.10.2009 and from the said wedlock a girl child is born. It is also not in dispute that parties are residing separately for the last more than 15 years.
use_in: divorce cases where parties have been living separately for a long time

legal_principles.principle: The court may not grant restitution of conjugal rights if the respondent has remarried and has children from the second marriage.
legal_principles.held: Under the circumstances, we are of the considered view that the prayer made by the appellant-wife for restitution of conjugal rights cannot be granted at this stage
use_in: divorce cases where the respondent has remarried and has children from the second marriage

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court are set aside.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petitions under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
